reports.title: All 44 Kano State LGAs 2025 Budgets (Kano Municipal Council 2025 Approved Budget)
reports.publisher: Kano State Government / Kano Municipal Council
reports.region: Kano Municipal LGA, Kano State, Nigeria
reports.description: A genuine LGA-specific budget spreadsheet, one of 44 individual per-LGA files Kano State's government hosts (not a state aggregate). Kano Municipal Council's own 2025 Approved Budget spreadsheet, verified by direct download and parse (openpyxl): "KANO MUNICIPAL COUNCIL / KANO STATE GOVERNMENT / SUMMARY OF THE APPROVED BUDGET FOR THE YEAR 2025." Named revenue lines for 2025: "Federal Allocation" (Approved Budget 4,586,665,421), "VAT" (6,582,776,098), "10% State Allocation" (100,000,000); "TOTAL REVENUE" 14,804,164,399. This is the closest primary document found in this branch to an actual named-LGA budget: state-hosted, but the underlying spreadsheet is Kano Municipal Council's own document, not a state-wide aggregate.
reports.cadence_note: Annual LGA budget; this is the 2025 edition, one of 44 parallel per-LGA files on the same state page.

reports.title: Total Net Revenue Performances of the Local Governments in Lagos State, Nigeria (Office of the Auditor-General for Local Governments)
reports.publisher: Office of the Auditor-General for Local Governments, Lagos State
reports.description: A Lagos State Auditor-General report naming individual LGA-level Statutory Allocation (FAAC-derived), Grant, and Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) figures for all 20 constitutionally-recognized Lagos LGAs (not the 37 non-constitutional LCDAs). Verified by direct PDF download and pdftotext extraction. Header: "OFFICE OF THE AUDITOR GENERAL FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENTS / TOTAL NET REVENUE PERFORMANCES OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS IN LAGOS STATE, NIGERIA." Sample rows: "8 Eti Osa ... 2,410,251,814.68 [Statutory Allocation] ... 31,297,500.00 [Grant] ... 881,197,063.51 [IGR]"; "11 Ikeja ... 2,444,544,619.96 [Statutory Allocation] ... 30,000,000.00 [Grant]". Underlying data year is 2020 per the filename; no explicit 'year ended' text appears in the extracted text itself.
reports.cadence_note: Annual Auditor-General report; this edition covers 2020 revenue performance.

reports.publisher: Office of the Auditor-General for Local Governments, Osun State
reports.description: Osun State's Auditor-General annual report, naming all 30 LGAs plus 1 LCDA with individual 2022 total-revenue figures in Note 1. Verified by direct PDF download. Cover: "REPORT OF THE AUDITOR-GENERAL FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENTS ON THE ACCOUNTS OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS IN OSUN STATE...FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31ST DECEMBER, 2022." Sample rows from the "NOTE 1 TOTAL REVENUE" table: "1 ATAKUMOSA EAST 1,952,411,283.41", "2 ATAKUMOSA WEST 2,010,886,099.75", "31 OSOGBO 2,224,355,093.00" (total across all LGAs: ₦61,755,309,709.66). Same document genre as Lagos's Auditor-General-for-Local-Governments report (ng-lagos-auditor-general-lg-2020) — a repeatable Nigerian state-government document type worth checking further in other states.
reports.cadence_note: Annual Auditor-General report; this edition covers the year ended 31 December 2022.

reports.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 — Section 162 (Federation Account) and Fourth Schedule (Functions of a Local Government Council)
reports.description: The constitutional root of Nigeria's three-tier revenue-sharing system. Verified via direct PDF download from a federal .gov.ng host (National Human Rights Commission). Section 162(3): "Any amount standing to the credit of the Federation Account shall be distributed among the Federal and State Governments and the Local Government Councils in each State on such terms and in such manner as may be prescribed by the National Assembly." Section 162(6): "Each State shall maintain a special account to be called 'State Joint Local Government Account' into which shall be paid all allocations to the Local Government Councils of the State from the Federation Account and from the Government of the State." Section 162(7): "Each State shall pay to Local Government Councils in its area of jurisdiction such proportion of its total revenue on such terms and in such manner as may be prescribed by the National Assembly." This document establishes the mechanism and obligation only — the actual vertical/horizontal percentages are prescribed by the Allocation of Revenue (Federation Account, etc.) Act (ng-allocation-of-revenue-act). CAVEAT: the source PDF has a recurring extraction artifact dropping the first 1-4 characters of many lines (confirmed via both pdftotext -layout and -raw, so likely a font/rendering issue in the source itself); only grammatically-complete lines were quoted.

dependencies.basis: Kano Municipal Council's own 2025 budget spreadsheet lists 'Federal Allocation' as a named revenue line (₦4,586,665,421) — the Federation Account distribution the Allocation of Revenue Act governs. The document names the revenue category but does not itself quote the Act's percentage formula, so 'cites' rather than 'calculated_from'.

The Lagos Auditor-General's report lists 'Statutory Allocation' as a distinct revenue column for each LGA — the State Joint Local Government Account's Federation Account-derived component, which the Allocation of Revenue Act governs the terms of. No formula/percentage is itself quoted in this report, so 'cites' rather than 'calculated_from'.

Section 162(3) directly anticipates the Allocation of Revenue Act by describing distribution 'on such terms and in such manner as may be prescribed by the National Assembly' — the Constitution establishes the obligation, the Act (already in corpus) supplies the actual formula.

_dropped.edge: Any individual Nigerian LGA's own website -> a self-published budget/financial-statement document
_dropped.why: Checked Ikeja LGA, Eti-Osa LGA (TLS certificate expired), Port Harcourt City LGA, and Abuja Municipal Area Council (site unreachable/robots-blocked) — none publish a budget or financial document on their own site. The genuine LGA-level documents that do exist (this file's three municipal nodes) are all STATE-hosted (Auditor-General reports, or a state government page distributing LGA budget files), not LGA-operated. FOLLOW-UP 2026-08-13 (Grok, same-day): independently re-checked amacfct.org.ng — confirmed genuine DNS NXDOMAIN (not a proxy-side block on this branch's own tooling), and a candidate alternate domain amacfct.com returns an SSL protocol error. AMAC appears to have no live official web presence at all under either domain, upgrading this from an access-method question to a reasonably confirmed absence of any AMAC-operated site.

_dropped.edge: RMAFC's own current allocation-formula percentages (52.68% / 26.72% / 20.60% vertical split) as a primary RMAFC-hosted document
_dropped.why: Re-confirmed this round: rmafc.gov.ng's own site describes the Allocation Department's function ('develops and applies allocation formulas and indices... determination of Vertical Revenue Allocation Formula for the sharing of revenue from the Federation Account') but does not publish the current percentages or a gazette document on any reachable page. No nass.gov.ng-hosted copy of the Constitution or Allocation of Revenue Act was found either — the best available .gov.ng host remains nigeriarights.gov.ng (NHRC), used for ng-constitution-1999-section162.

Unlike the Lagos and Kano documents, Osun's Auditor-General report's Note 1 table gives only a bare 'TOTAL REVENUE' figure per LGA, without breaking out a named 'Statutory Allocation' or 'Federal Allocation' line — no citation of the Allocation of Revenue Act or FAAC by name was found in the extracted text, so no edge is drawn from this specific document.
